import numpy as np
belief = np.ones(10) / 10
motion = np.roll(belief, 1) * 0.8 + belief * 0.2  # prediction
sensor = np.array([0.9 if i==3 else 0.1 for i in range(10)])
belief = sensor * motion
belief /= belief.sum()
print("Most probable location:", np.argmax(belief))
description: You can follow prediction and sensor weighting over ten locations.

steps.description: belief starts uniform across ten positions. You mix a one-position roll with the original array to form motion.
The sensor array assigns 0.9 to index 3 and 0.1 elsewhere. You multiply those likelihood weights by motion element by element.

steps.answer: It normalizes them so the belief entries sum to one while preserving their relative sizes.
steps.question: What does dividing by belief.sum() do to the weights?

steps.description: argmax selects the largest normalized entry. You see Most probable location: 3 in the output.
